initial_requirements: Tarrant County needs an integrated justice capability to improve the administration of indigent defense services and information sharing across the criminal justice community. The system should help the Office of Attorney Appointments receive and process requests for appointed counsel, obtain relevant defendant and case information, coordinate attorney appointments, and notify the people and justice organizations involved in each request.

messages.content:
Hello, I’m GPTREI, your requirements elicitation assistant. I’ll be gathering detailed information about Tarrant County Indigent Defense Services so we can understand the needs clearly and support the right solution.

Before we begin, are my assumptions about the scope of this interview aligned with your expectations, or would you like to define a different focus?

Yes, that scope sounds right to me. We’re mainly focused on how the system should support attorney appointment requests, case and defendant information sharing, coordination across the justice partners, and notifications to the involved parties. If we need to get more specific later, I can help with the workflow details and any constraints we have in practice.
To start off, could you please introduce yourself and your connection to this project?

I’m speaking as someone involved in the administration of indigent defense services for Tarrant County, especially around attorney appointments and the related coordination with courts and justice partners. My perspective is focused on making sure the process is efficient, accurate, and that the right people get the right information at the right time.
Thank you. Could you briefly describe the current process or system you use today for receiving, reviewing, and acting on appointed-counsel requests?

Right now, the process is fairly manual and spread across a few different systems and communications. Requests come in with case details and defendant information, and staff have to review them, verify what they can, and then coordinate the appointment with the appropriate attorney and notify the involved parties. It works, but it can be slow because people are often checking multiple sources and following up by phone or email.
What current processes do you want to change or improve, or what features are you hoping to get from this project?

We want to reduce the manual back-and-forth and get the needed case information into one place faster. A big goal is better coordination so attorney appointments can happen more smoothly, and notifications can go out automatically instead of relying so much on staff to chase everyone down. We also want more consistent information sharing across the justice community so there are fewer delays and fewer errors.
Based on your description, should the project also include a shared view of request status so staff and justice partners can see where each appointment request is in the process?

Yes, that would be very helpful. Having a shared status view would let our staff and the other justice partners see whether a request is pending, being reviewed, assigned, or completed without having to call around for updates. That kind of visibility would probably cut down on a lot of confusion and duplicate work.

Are there any other main features or functions you’d like to see in this project, beyond request intake, shared status visibility, coordination of attorney appointments, information sharing, and automated notifications?

I think those are the core pieces, but I’d also want good search and tracking so staff can quickly find prior requests, appointments, and related case history. It would also be useful if the system could keep an audit trail of what changed and who made the change, since that matters for accountability. If there’s room, some basic reporting would help us understand volumes, turnaround times, and where things are getting delayed.

So the main features/functions we’ve identified are request intake and processing, shared request status visibility, coordination of attorney appointments, case and defendant information sharing, automated notifications, search and tracking, audit trail, and basic reporting. Is that correct?
Yes, that’s a good summary of the main things we’ve talked about. That matches what we need at a high level.
Which of those features would you say are the highest priority to deliver first?

The highest priorities would be request intake and processing, coordination of attorney appointments, and access to the case and defendant information needed to make those decisions. After that, shared status visibility and automated notifications would be next because they really help keep everyone aligned. Search, audit trail, and reporting are important too, but I’d see those as secondary to getting the core workflow working well first.
Please describe what you want request intake and processing to accomplish, and how a request should move through the workflow from submission to appointment.

At a minimum, the system should capture the request, validate the basic information, and route it to the right staff for review. From there, the request should move through checking defendant and case details, determining eligibility or appointment needs, assigning counsel, and then sending out the appropriate notices. If something is missing or unclear, it should be easy to flag the request for follow-up instead of just leaving it in limbo.
Could you describe the request intake and processing workflow step-by-step, from the moment a request is submitted until the appointment is finalized?

A request comes in, and the system should record who submitted it, when it was submitted, and the key case and defendant details. Then staff review it for completeness and verify the information they need to make the appointment decision, including any linked case information. If everything checks out, the appointment is assigned and the relevant parties are notified; if not, it goes back for correction or follow-up until it can be finalized.
